claims: PBRT CPU PathIntegrator and Guo pathwsampler both include NEE power weights and the complementary BSDF-hit emitter term. The former engine analytic sphere route lacked that hit term; this is an omitted estimator contribution, not merely a different valid MIS policy.

Existing engine power-CDF selection PMFs, power heuristic, uniform sphere-area sampling and radiance conversion remain unchanged. The references may use projected-cone sphere sampling; that valid difference can change variance and is retained.
The PBRT evidence here is PathIntegrator only. PBRT VolPath spectral/ratio MIS is a separate estimator; this audit does not claim identical policies across all integrators or renderers.

Analytic spheres are black opaque emitting geometry, matching the authored Guo spheres whose omitted BSDF defaults to zero-reflectance diffuse. Front hits emit, inside/back hits block with zero emission.

The nearest analytic sphere is found over the original RayDesc interval before alpha traversal; a copy clips TLAS traversal to its distance. A nearer accepted mesh or boundary wins, exact equal distance chooses one analytic endpoint. No epsilon tie merges distinct surfaces.

Medium transport first reaches the provisional nearest mesh/sphere endpoint or scatters earlier. Pure boundaries preserve the previous scattering vertex and remaining full ray range. Sphere emission uses the updated medium throughput.

The analytic PDF uses exact sphere identity, actual selection PMF, the same unclamped 1/(4*pi*r*r) area density and near-field rejection support as NEE. It does not use the 1e-3 positional mesh matching tolerance.

Shadow connections test analytic opaque spheres in their existing [TMin, target-distance-PT_RAY_EPS] interval. The sampled endpoint is excluded, while other spheres and zero-flux/back-facing spheres block. Existing boundary/medium traversal remains in use for unblocked connections.

GetSceneRayLength also encloses the current sphere centers/radii from g_Lights. All existing camera/continuation/phase/environment-directional shadow call sites use this helper, avoiding stale CPU draw-only bounds on light-radius edits.

A paired emissive mesh and LightComponent do not create two CDF entries: the CDF enumerates LightComponents only. A single nearest endpoint prevents adding the paired mesh and analytic emission simultaneously. No arbitrary nearby geometry or faceted proxy is removed.

Exactly coincident SphereLight components are separate additive emission terms at one opaque endpoint. Each term uses its own unchanged NEE selection PMF and complementary hit weight; no summed-PMF mixture silently replaces the existing component estimators.

Only sphere analytic transport is repaired. Disk/tube/area analytic intersection policies, normal interpolation, material/BSDF/ray-cone behavior and source scene assets are unchanged. The existing Killeroo normal-field discrepancy remains separately open.
